name: P-ARC
notes: Cells can exceed Python's default csv.field_size_limit (~128 KiB); call csv.field_size_limit(sys.maxsize) before reading the CSV.
tasks/<task_id>.json holds each task's train and test pairs in the standard ARC JSON format.

columns.name: task_name
columns.description: Short descriptive name of the task, e.g. corner_to_center.

columns.name: rule
columns.description: Natural-language statement of the task's intended rule, reviewed by the authors.

columns.name: rule_source
columns.description: How the rule was written: human_reviewed (redrafted from the task's transform and reviewed), human_annotated (written from scratch), or draft (the original hand-written rule, kept after review).

columns.name: train_demonstrations_json
columns.description: Compact JSON array of training pairs {input, output}; grids are lists of lists of integers 0-9.

columns.name: test_input_json
columns.description: Compact JSON grid for the held-out test input.

columns.name: test_output_json
columns.description: Compact JSON grid for the held-out test output.

columns.name: stable_instances_50_json
columns.description: Compact JSON object {"train": [...]} with 50 fixed generator-produced {input, output} pairs.

columns.name: human_corruptions_json
columns.description: Compact JSON array of 3 {input, output} pairs with incorrect outputs, made by people: erroneous attempts from the feasibility check or errors designed by the task's creator.

columns.name: generator_py
columns.description: Python source of the task's generator.

columns.name: verifier_py
columns.description: Python source of the task's verifier, which maps an input grid to the correct output grid.
